matches.quote: Several factors independently modify h_E, h_x, h_y and switching behaviour, and could create pinning sites with or without a twist: ... transfer-induced strain
one device at one angle cannot support "twist-tuned" exchange... Required controls... several devices; at least two or three further twist angles
The gradual, multi-step transitions at spots 2 and 3 (Fig. 4c,d) are assigned to a canted state. They are equally consistent with spatially averaged mixed AP/P domains
h_y rises from 1.06 T (pristine) to 1.42–1.61 T (twisted)... and is not expected to change by ~50% with twist.
The extracted anisotropies change too much to support "twisting primarily tunes interlayer exchange"... acknowledge that the twist (or interface) modifies more than h_E.
The variation across spots a few µm apart could equally reflect: - inhomogeneous interlayer contact; - bubbles; - local twist-angle disorder; - strain.
The optical probe cannot distinguish monodomain switching from multidomain reversal, or a canted state from mixed AP/P domains.
acquire field-dependent hyperspectral PL/reflectance maps across the twisted region with sub-µm steps, correlated with topography, bubbles and strain.
Confocal PL averages over a ~1 µm spot, i.e. ~10⁴ moiré cells... "Coherent moiré averaging" is assumed, not demonstrated
A simpler alternative explanation, in which the twist adds coercivity rather than mainly reducing exchange, is not considered... giving a loop centred at the exchange field with width 2h_c.
The manuscript provides none of the following: ... a comparison of the ~47% h_E reduction with the averaged J(r) from first principles.
include micromagnetic or atomistic simulations of the moiré bilayer showing that textures are suppressed at 3°, that the measured effective h_E results
The loop width is set by h_AP+ − h_P−, and the model's predicted AP→P field h_AP+ disagrees strongly with experiment

notes: C10 is judged 'partly' because the review identifies the same multi-step switching at spots 2 and 3 as evidence for mixed AP/P domains (P12) and mentions minor loops in P23, but asks for PL spectral lineshape analysis and magnetic imaging at spots 2 and 3 rather than minor loops at spot 3 specifically. C17 and C16 are judged 'partly' because the review addresses the same underlying anomalies via the extracted anisotropies h_y and h_x (P2, P7, P14) and coercivity h_c (P24) rather than framing them as R2's questions. C11 is judged 'partly' because the review raises intralayer moiré spin textures (P10), spatially varying J_inter(r) simulations for the switching-field discrepancy (P20), and inhomogeneous states in Fig. 4c,d (P12) across three points rather than attributing all three to a single small-angle noncollinear texture.
